title: A/P Unpaid Invoices: a vendor credit stays at the bottom when Due Date is sorted
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a vendor, vendor A, with two overdue bills, bill A (due 10 days ago) and bill B (due 20 days ago), and one unused vendor credit, vendor credit A, on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/P Unpaid Invoices (Reports, then "A/P Unpaid Invoices" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu; the page title reads "A/P Unpaid Invoices Report").
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Expand vendor A's group.
  2. Click the "Due Date" header.
  3. Click the "Due Date" header again.
  4. Click the "Past Due" header.
  5. Click the "Past Due" header again.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The group shows the two bills and the vendor credit.
  • Vendor credit A's Due Date and Past Due cells hold no date or number (the screen draws a dash, "—"): a vendor credit has no due date and no Past Due here.

Step 2:

  • Bill B, then bill A, then vendor credit A at the bottom of the group.

Step 3:

  • Bill A, then bill B.
  • Vendor credit A still at the bottom.

Step 4:

  • Bill B (20 days), then bill A (10 days), then vendor credit A at the bottom.

Step 5:

  • Bill A, then bill B.
  • Vendor credit A still at the bottom.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R6: “A blank value (for example a vendor credit on A/P Unpaid Invoices, which has no due date and no Past Due) sorts to the bottom of its group in both directions. On A/P Detail a vendor credit shows its own date as its due date, as today, so it is not blank there.”
  • S2-R2: “The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4). The second click reverses it. The third click repeats the first; there is no unsorted state.”
